analysis_notes.intensity_method: Joint Gaussian peak fits at all 18 tabulated centers with a linear baseline for each spectrum. Widths were shared across temperatures within each technique; peak amplitudes were fitted independently. Integrated areas were calibrated separately for each band and Raman wavelength against susceptibility-derived LS or HS populations using one multiplicative response factor and no additive population offset. Reported band fractions average the independent 532 and 785 nm estimates; each wavelength independently passes monotonicity and the 0.10 tolerance.
analysis_notes.overall_fractions: The reported overall fractions are the susceptibility-derived total high-spin fractions; neither measured endpoint is treated as a pure state.
analysis_notes.both_states: B07, B10 and B15 retain substantial fitted Raman intensity in both extrapolated pure states, with wavelength-dependent LS/HS response ratios. Their total band intensities are not pure-state population markers.
analysis_notes.activity_interpretation: Low-spin activities are assignments based on the dominant extrapolated low-spin response and centrosymmetric mutual exclusion. Weak opposite-technique features are treated as distinct coincident modes or extrinsic signal, rather than intrinsic dual activity. The supplied data do not independently establish the origin of those weak features; these intrinsic activity assignments are conditional on this interpretation.
analysis_notes.breathing_assignment: B01 at 233 cm-1 is assigned as the best-supported breathing-mode candidate: a strong low-frequency LS Raman feature at all three excitation wavelengths, a much weaker IR response, and population tracking consistent with susceptibility. B06 at 534 cm-1 instead tracks HS. The available unpolarized spectra and competing labels do not uniquely prove the normal-mode eigenvector or totally symmetric character of B01.
analysis_notes.unresolved: B18 has a weak nearly temperature-independent fitted area, with scatter comparable to any population-dependent change; the data cannot distinguish a BOTH band from background or a weak combination feature.
